description: From a naked-eye perspective, stars are stable and predictable. Not much goes on but shining. The sun itself is fairly plain and nondescript and will shine relatively steadily for billions of years. It's considered a low-mass star compared to the most massive stars, which are rarer and contain many times its mass.
title: Why aging stars suffer a sudden luminosity dip

description: In the Late Iron Age, or post-Talayotic period, over 2,000 years ago, Menorca and the other Balearic Islands experienced increasing connectivity with the wider Mediterranean. However, they also maintained distinctive local funerary traditions, such as burying their loved ones in rock-cut tombs, or artificial caves. Some of these caves contained external courtyards located in front of the burial chambers where animal offerings might have been made. Archaeologists even suspect that perishable foods or liquids were offered in characteristic island containers, such as high-bottomed vessels. Until now, however, the contents of these ceramic containers had never been identified.
title: Milk and wine used in Menorcan funerary rituals over 2,000 years ago

description: Where segregation is high, the school a child attends is closely linked to how many years of education parents expect their child to go on to complete.
title: School environment plays key role in shaping parents' educational hopes for their children, suggests study

description: Radiocarbon dating and isotope analysis of an immaculately preserved skeleton from Mesolithic Denmark indicate that the individual lived through the introduction of agriculture and adapted his diet to the change, providing a unique "eyewitness account" of one of humanity's most significant technological revolutions.
title: Archaeologists uncover a witness to the Neolithic revolution

description: Megafauna remains, stone tools and rare plant material recovered from the 125,000-year-old lakeside site of Uruq al-Julaybah in Mundafan, southern Saudi Arabia, provide one of the most detailed pictures yet of prehistoric human life in Arabia. Together, the discoveries reveal how early people lived, hunted and used their environment during a greener, wetter period in Arabian history.
title: When the Saudi desert was green: A 125,000-year-old lakeside reveals how early humans lived

description: UBC researchers have helped uncover 15,000 new potential strong gravitational lenses—the largest collection of these cosmic tools that help astronomers investigate dark matter.
title: Dark matter–hunting satellite Euclid reveals record number of cosmic 'magnifying glasses'

description: Tsunamis triggered by volcanic eruptions are poorly understood because of the complex dynamics governing how falling rocks and ash interact with seawater to generate waves. As a result, it is difficult to anticipate whether a volcanic flow will trigger a tsunami and, if so, how big it will be. Researchers have used laboratory experiments to study this process, but little is known about how well these models mimic reality.
title: The experiments improving our understanding of volcanic tsunamis

description: When a cloud of atoms is cooled close to absolute zero, its atoms can merge into a Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC): an exotic fluid in which atoms across the whole cloud share a single quantum state. Current theories predict that as a disordered quantum gas settles into this ordered state, a tangle of tiny vortices should form and gradually unravel.
title: Tangled quantum whirlpools caught unraveling in an ultracold gas

description: Global temperatures may continue to rise even after human CO₂ emissions stop. The temperature change that follows is known as the zero emissions commitment (ZEC), and it is often assumed to be close to zero. A study led by the Met Office Hadley Center, with co-authors from several institutions including the University of Liverpool, found that the temperature response depends on how much warming has already occurred.
title: Climate response: Why previous warming makes all the difference

description: An international team of paleontologists, including researchers from McGill University, has discovered "remarkably large" rodent fossils in the pit of a mine in southern Thailand. The finding, published in Scientific Reports, provides a new perspective on the early manifestation of rodent gigantism—the process by which animals evolve to become larger—demonstrating that the evolutionary history of large-bodied rodents is considerably older and more geographically widespread than previously recognized, the researchers said.
title: Giant, prehistoric rodent fossils discovered in southern Thailand

description: A recent reanalysis of the outsize black hole galaxy UHZ1 using existing X-ray data and new infrared observations challenges a previous groundbreaking claim. Three years ago, this galaxy made news for hosting an unusually massive and heavily dust-obscured black hole formed through direct collapse. Led by Fan Zou of the University of Michigan, the new study reports no signs of hidden black hole activity. The paper, published in The Astrophysical Journal on Oct. 14, suggests UHZ1 could be a low-mass, metal-poor, star-forming galaxy.
title: New observations challenge evidence for an 'outsize' black hole in the early universe

description: Indigenous farmer Banu Ismahasan walks through a golden field of tall stalks in southeastern Taiwan, harvesting by hand the grain heads of an ancient crop resistant to extreme weather.
title: Taiwan Indigenous farmer revives climate-resilient millet

description: For a decade, the 1.5C goal has served as the north star of climate action, a line nations pledged to hold to avoid the worst ravages of a warming planet.
title: Nations grapple with loss of 1.5C target at UN climate summit

description: SpaceX's Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.
title: SpaceX's Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first

description: Astronomers have revealed three dense cores at different evolutionary stages within the massive star-forming region G40.282−0.219, shedding light on the physical and chemical differences among cores within the same massive dense clump.
title: ALMA reveals three star-forming cores at different stages inside one gas clump
